title: Split the Array
statement: You receive an integer array `nums` whose length is even. Decide whether its elements can be divided into two groups `nums1` and `nums2` of exactly `nums.length / 2` elements each, where every element of `nums` goes into exactly one group and neither group holds the same value twice. Return `true` if such a division exists and `false` if it does not.
notes:
## Intuition

Each half may hold a value at most once, so any value can appear at most twice in total: one copy per half. If some value appears three or more times, two copies must land in the same half and the split fails. When every value appears at most twice, a split always exists: put one copy of each duplicated value in each half, then share out the single copies so both halves reach `nums.length / 2`. Searching over all splits is exponential, but counting copies settles the question in one pass.

## Approach

1. Keep a map `count` from each value to how many copies have been seen.
2. For each `value` in `nums`, compute `copies`, its count including this one.
3. If `copies` exceeds 2, return `false` at once.
4. Otherwise store `copies` and continue.
5. If the loop ends, no value appears more than twice, so return `true`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4]`. The counts grow to `1 → 2`, `2 → 2`, `3 → 1` and `4 → 1`; `copies` never goes above 2, so the answer is `true` (for instance `[1, 2, 3]` and `[1, 2, 4]`).

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one map update per element.
- Space: O(n) for the map (at most 100 distinct values here, so an array of size 101 works too).

## Pitfalls

- The number of distinct values does not matter on its own; only a value with three or more copies breaks the split.
- Both halves must have the same size, but the even length already guarantees it whenever every count is at most 2.
- Checking only adjacent duplicates is wrong unless the array is sorted first.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | copies seen so far of each value |
| `value` | the current element |
| `copies` | how many times `value` has appeared, including now |

narration.2: Prepare a map from each value to how many copies have been seen.
narration.4: Look at the elements one at a time.
narration.5: Count this copy of the value.
narration.6: A third copy would force two equal values into the same half...
narration.9: Remember the new count for this value.
narration.11: No value appears more than twice, so one copy can go in each half.
